1	/**
2	 * A pi resource loader that reads nothing from disk.
3	 *
4	 * pi's `DefaultResourceLoader` auto-discovers extensions, prompt templates,
5	 * skills, themes, context files and SYSTEM.md from `cwd` and `agentDir`, all
6	 * enabled by default. Those are the right defaults for a developer running pi
7	 * in their own repo. They are the wrong defaults for us: our `cwd` is the
8	 * agent's workspace — written to by the agent's own `write`/`bash` tools, and
9	 * kept across runs for the pod's lifetime (nothing removes it; the workspaces
10	 * volume is pod-local, not a PVC) — so each of those paths is agent-controlled
11	 * input to the NEXT run:
12	 *
13	 * - `<cwd>/.pi/extensions/*.{ts,js}` are `jiti.import`ed and EXECUTED inside the
14	 *   worker process, bypassing the bash command policy and the `buildAgentEnv`
15	 *   environment allowlist entirely.
16	 * - `<cwd>/.pi/prompts/*.md` replace a user message beginning with `/<name>`.
17	 * - `<cwd>/.pi/SYSTEM.md` replaces the whole system prompt; `APPEND_SYSTEM.md`
18	 *   appends to it.
19	 * - `<cwd>/.pi/skills`, the ancestor `.agents/skills` walk (shared by every
20	 *   conversation under one workspace root), and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` all
21	 *   feed the prompt.
22	 *
23	 * `DefaultResourceLoader`'s suppression options would leave the property
24	 * resting on several flags and overrides, and they only discard results AFTER
25	 * `reload()` has already walked the tree via the package manager. That walk
26	 * recurses into subdirectories and follows symlinks (`collectSkillEntries`
27	 * stats the link target and recurses when it is a directory), so the agent
28	 * still gets to decide how much work every later boot of the conversation does.
29	 * (A symlink cycle does not hang: the recursion overflows the stack and
30	 * `collectSkillEntries`'s own catch-all swallows it. Measured, not assumed.)
31	 *
32	 * So this implements pi's `ResourceLoader` interface with no filesystem access
33	 * at all. Everything Lobu wants the agent to have — skills, platform/network
34	 * instructions, MCP servers — arrives from the gateway as session context, so
35	 * there is nothing legitimate to discover here.
36	 *
37	 * The coupling to pi is the exported `ResourceLoader` interface: if a future pi
38	 * adds a method, this fails at compile time rather than silently reopening a
39	 * discovery path.
40	 */
41	import {
42	  createExtensionRuntime,
43	  type LoadExtensionsResult,
44	  type ResourceLoader,
45	} from "@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent";
46	
47	export function createLobuResourceLoader(): ResourceLoader {
48	  // Built once, not per call: `AgentSession._buildRuntime` reads this result and
49	  // writes extension flag values onto `runtime`, which a fresh object per call
50	  // would silently discard.
51	  const extensions: LoadExtensionsResult = {
52	    extensions: [],
53	    errors: [],
54	    runtime: createExtensionRuntime(),
55	  };
56	
57	  return {
58	    getExtensions: () => extensions,
59	    getSkills: () => ({ skills: [], diagnostics: [] }),
60	    getPrompts: () => ({ prompts: [], diagnostics: [] }),
61	    getThemes: () => ({ themes: [], diagnostics: [] }),
62	    getAgentsFiles: () => ({ agentsFiles: [] }),
63	    getSystemPrompt: () => undefined,
64	    getAppendSystemPrompt: () => [],
65	    extendResources: () => {
66	      // pi calls this when an extension's `resources_discover` hook returns
67	      // paths. With no extensions loaded it never fires; ignoring the paths
68	      // keeps the "nothing is read from disk" property even if one is added.
69	    },
70	    reload: async () => {
71	      // Nothing to re-read: every getter above is a constant.
72	    },
73	  };
74	}

content.text:
Short answer: not yet — and one thing I found changes the risk calculus.

**This isn't the cleanup we scoped. It's a live P0.** The worker assigns its assembled system prompt once after building the session. `AgentSession.prompt()` reassigns `agent.state.systemPrompt` on *every* call — to whatever a `before_agent_start` handler returns, or back to pi's base prompt when nothing returns one. Lobu registered no handler, so the assignment was overwritten before the first request was ever built.

I proved it by reading the outgoing provider request, not the composed string:

```
=== WHAT THE MODEL RECEIVED (before fix) ===
contains Lobu prompt:  false
contains pi opener:    true
contains pi docs block: true
```

So in production every agent has been running on pi's stock *"You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness"* prompt — no identity, no soulMd/userMd, no platform instructions, no MCP server instructions, no memory guidance, no network section, plus a pi documentation block pointing at `node_modules` paths that don't exist in the worker image. That's the real answer to "why does the agent get pi docs?" — the regex was never the problem, its output just never arrived.

Fixed natively: the resource loader supplies the document as pi's `customPrompt`, and a hand-built synthetic `before_agent_start` extension reinstalls it each turn. No regex, no mutation of pi internals. `replaceBasePromptIdentity` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_OPENER_RE` are deleted.

**On confidence:** high (90) that delivery is fixed — mutation 4 restores the old assign-once shape and 4 tests fail; restoring each seam individually fails its own tests. But only medium (65) on prompt *content* in production, and that's the number that matters here: this changes the system prompt for every agent in the fleet, and I have not booted the app and driven a real conversation. Everything so far is a stubbed provider endpoint.

**On admin-merging:** yes once the required checks report green — that's your normal step 9, and I'll do it without asking. What I won't do is `--admin` past a check that hasn't reported. But I'd rather not merge on today's evidence at all, because the blast radius is every agent and my verification is offline. One real boot converts that 65 into a real number and costs maybe fifteen minutes.

Also worth knowing: `make review-fix` is still running and has already edited the working tree — it caught a genuine defect in my first version (the base prompt carried `Current date:`/`Current working directory:` twice, since pi appends its own pair to a `customPrompt`). I'll verify its full diff before trusting any of it.

Plan I'm continuing with unless you redirect: let review-fix finish, verify its diff, re-run gates, push and open the PR, `make review` once, boot the worktree and drive one real agent turn to see the actual prompt, then admin-merge on green.

You have persistent memory. Use it proactively — don't wait to be asked.

When asked about the workspace's data — including people, leads, companies, connections, feeds, runs, or counts — query it before answering. commit 30a4bd836fefb14569e20e7edac7e1055f5c9b7a
Author: Burak Emre Kabakcı <emrekabakci@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 29 17:13:13 2026 +0100

    fix(server): tell every chat agent it is a participant, not an observer (#2318)
    
    * fix(server): tell every chat agent it is a participant, not an observer
    
    A chat agent needs two facts nothing else in the prompt supplies: who it
    is in the conversation, and that the messages it receives are addressed
    to it. Only Slack supplied them — `createPlatformAdapter` attached an
    instruction provider solely when the platform descriptor declared one,
    and Slack is the only descriptor that does. Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp,
    Teams and Google Chat got an empty `platformInstructions`.
    
    With that gap the agent has only its identity markdown, which describes
    the principal in the third person ("you work on the user's data on their
    behalf") and never says the person currently typing IS that principal.
    The model resolves the ambiguity per turn, and often the wrong way: it
    treats the inbound message as observed conversation about a third party
    and narrates it back — "Burak is asking if REVERTCHECK is working. How
    would you like to respond?" — addressing an operator who does not exist.
    
    Make identity the default for every chat platform rather than a
    per-platform opt-in, so a new platform inherits it instead of
    re-deriving it. Slack keeps only its genuine delta, `<@U…>` mention
    encoding, and inherits the rest.
    
    Identity is best-effort: `Adapter.botUserId` is optional in the Chat SDK
    and some platforms carry no handle, so the participation framing is
    emitted even when no handle resolves — that is the half that fixes the
    voice. The only case that emits nothing is a missing org, which is the
    cross-tenant guard.
    
    Prompt-cache safe: the block is connection-scoped (platform, handle, bot
    id) and sits at the front of `gatewayInstructions`, where the
    openai-completions path caches by longest common prefix with no explicit
    breakpoints. A test renders it for two users/sessions on one connection
    and asserts byte equality, so a later conversation-scoped interpolation
    fails the build instead of silently costing the cache on every new
    conversation.
    
    * test(server): update Slack instruction provider test to the shared identity contract
    
    * docs(server): record why chat identity degrades and why the block is cache-scoped
    
    Restores two things the fixer pass removed: the reasoning for the
    prompt-cache contract (a conversation-scoped interpolation here silently
    forfeits the cache for every new conversation on the connection), and
    the note that identity is best-effort while the participation framing is
    not.
    
    Pins the degradation with a test: identity resolution has no agent+platform
    fallback because there is one InstructionContext construction site and it
    always carries the signed connectionId, so a missing field drops the handle
    but must still emit the framing.

fix(agent-worker): deliver Lobu's system prompt to the model

The worker assembled a system prompt — agent identity, identityMd/soulMd/
userMd, platform instructions, MCP server instructions, memory guidance,
network access, skills, runtime shell — and assigned it once to
`session.agent.state.systemPrompt` after constructing the session.

`AgentSession.prompt()` reassigns that field on EVERY call: to whatever a
`before_agent_start` handler returns, or, when no handler returns one, back
to pi's own base prompt. Lobu registered no handler, so the assignment was
overwritten before the first request was ever built. Every agent ran on
pi's stock "expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent
harness" prompt plus a documentation block describing pi's SDK, extensions
and TUI, pointing at node_modules paths that do not exist in the worker
image. None of the composed prompt reached the model.

Install it through the two seams pi actually consults: the resource
loader's `getSystemPrompt()` (pi's `customPrompt`, which replaces the
default rather than competing with it) and a synthetic `before_agent_start`
extension built in memory, which survives the per-turn reset. Both call one
renderer, so the base and per-turn documents cannot drift; the loader is
also the fail-safe, since the extension runner swallows handler errors — a
broken handler degrades to a Lobu prompt without the tools section rather
than to pi's.

Pi keeps ownership of what is genuinely pi's: the one-line tool snippets
and per-tool guideline bullets, read live from `systemPromptOptions` rather
than copied, so a pi change cannot fork them silently.

Deletes `replaceBasePromptIdentity` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_OPENER_RE`. Lobu
no longer patches pi's prompt text; it supplies the document.

The regression test reads the outgoing provider request. Every earlier
prompt test asserted the string the worker *composed*, which is a different
question, and that difference is what hid this.

## Summary

- The worker assembled a system prompt — agent identity, `identityMd`/`soulMd`/`userMd`, platform instructions, MCP server instructions, memory guidance, network access, skills, runtime shell — and assigned it once to `session.agent.state.systemPrompt` after constructing the session. `AgentSession.prompt()` reassigns that field on **every** call: to whatever a `before_agent_start` handler returns, or, when no handler returns one, back to pi's own base prompt. Lobu registered no handler, so the assignment was overwritten before the first request was ever built.
- Net effect in production: every agent ran on pi's stock *"expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness"* prompt, plus a documentation block describing pi's SDK/extensions/TUI and pointing at `node_modules` paths that do not exist in the worker image. None of the composed prompt reached the model. This is the actual cause of "why does the agent get pi docs?" — the old regex worked; its output just never arrived.
- Fix installs the document through the two seams pi actually consults: the resource loader's `getSystemPrompt()` (pi's `customPrompt`, which *replaces* the default rather than competing with it) and a synthetic `before_agent_start` extension built in memory, which survives the per-turn reset. Both call one renderer, so base and per-turn documents cannot drift. The loader doubles as the fail-safe — pi's extension runner swallows handler errors, so a broken handler degrades to a Lobu prompt without the tool section rather than to pi's.
- Deletes `replaceBasePromptIdentity` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_OPENER_RE`. Lobu no longer patches pi's prompt text; it supplies the document. Pi keeps what is genuinely pi's — per-tool snippets and guideline bullets, read live from `systemPromptOptions` rather than copied, so a pi change cannot fork them silently.

## Test plan
- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming + gateway-llm)
- [x] Tests run: `make test-unit`, `bun test` in `packages/agent-worker` (808 pass / 12 skip / 0 fail across 55 files)

## Notes

- Third and last PR of the series: #2313 (stop pi discovering resources from the agent-writable workspace) → #2317 (gateway sends `identityMd`/`soulMd`/`userMd` separately) → this one.
- #2318 is currently inert in production for this same reason: its new participation block is appended to `gatewayInstructions`, which is part of the payload that was being discarded before every turn. It starts working when this merges.
- Blast radius is every agent in the fleet, since this changes what the model receives on every turn. Verification so far is a real `session.prompt()` against a stubbed provider endpoint; a live boot check is worth doing before/after rollout.

Here's where things stand.

**PR #2319 is open** — https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2319

The diff is exactly the 9 intended paths, verified against `origin/main` after rebase:

```
R  __tests__/replace-base-prompt-identity.test.ts -> agent-identity.test.ts
M  __tests__/pi-resource-discovery.test.ts
D  __tests__/prompt-assembly-smoke.test.ts
A  __tests__/system-prompt-builder.test.ts
A  __tests__/system-prompt-delivery.test.ts
M  runtime/pi-resources.ts
M  runtime/session-runner.ts
A  runtime/system-prompt.ts
M  runtime/worker.ts
```

Red→green is in the PR body, both reproduced against the committed code this session — the pre-fix wiring delivers `Lobu prompt: false / pi opener: true / pi docs: true`, the delivery suite gives 6 pass / 0 fail.

Two things I got beyond what I had before:

I dumped the actual document on the wire for a realistic input. It reads correctly — identity first, pi's live per-tool guidelines intact (including the `edits[].oldText` semantics that would have been forked if I'd copied them), then the gateway tail, then date and cwd. No pi opener, no docs block, no `node_modules`.

And `grep -n systemPrompt session-runner.ts` shows no residual `agent.state.systemPrompt` assignment anywhere — the only remaining hits are the memory-flush config, which is a user-message prefix.

`make review-fix` caught one real defect I'd introduced: my renderer always appended date and cwd, so on the loader/`customPrompt` path pi appended a second copy. It split the body out and now returns body-only there. There's a wire-level assertion pinning it (`split("Current date:").length - 1 === 1`).

**Confidence: 88.** Basis: the delivery assertion reads the outgoing provider request rather than the composed string, RED and GREEN both reproduced against committed code, 808 agent-worker tests pass, `make test-unit` exit 0, all 6 pre-pr gates clean, and I've now read the rendered document rather than inferring it. What keeps it off 95 is that `runAISession`'s own wiring — `resolveAgentIdentity(context.agentLayers)` and `finalInstructionsUpdated` feeding the renderer — is covered by typecheck and code reading, not by a booted gateway run.

On the merge question: `pi-review` and the four test jobs are still pending, so nothing is mergeable yet. I've got a background watch on the required checks. Once they report green I'll admin-squash without asking — that's the normal flow — but I won't `--admin` past anything that hasn't reported.

Next actions once it lands:
1. Prod-verify after rollout, gated on the squash commit via `gh pr view 2319 --json mergeCommit`. Prompt content isn't externally observable, so the check is a real agent turn in prod — the tell is whether it still narrates in the third person, since #2318's participation block only starts working when this merges.
2. Consider whether #2318 needs re-verifying in prod; my read is it's been inert since it merged, for this same reason.
3. Update the `system-prompt-override-is-inert` memory — it recorded the symptom but not this root cause.

name: project-system-prompt-override-is-inert
description: "pi resets agent.state.systemPrompt on EVERY prompt() — lobu's replaceBasePromptIdentity assignment is discarded before the first model call"
metadata:

---

`packages/agent-worker/src/runtime/session-runner.ts:1309` assigns
`session.agent.state.systemPrompt = finalSystemPrompt` once after
`buildAgentSession()`. pi 0.73.x `AgentSession.prompt()` unconditionally does
`this.agent.state.systemPrompt = this._baseSystemPrompt` (agent-session.js:797)
unless a **pi extension** `before_agent_start` handler returns a systemPrompt.
Lobu registers no such extension — its `runtimePluginHost.beforeAgentStart`
(session-runner.ts:1715) only prepends to the USER prompt. So the Lobu identity
AND the gateway tail (platform + MCP-server instructions) are wiped before the
first model call; the model sees pi's stock "expert coding assistant operating
inside pi" prompt. Verified 2026-07-29 by booting a real pi session, setting a
marker, calling prompt() — marker gone.

`prompt-assembly-smoke.test.ts` passes because it asserts on the assembled
string, never on `session.systemPrompt` after a prompt() turn — an instance of
[[feedback-test-the-shape-production-throws]].

**Why:** the supported override exists — `createAgentSession({ resourceLoader })`
with `new DefaultResourceLoader({ cwd, agentDir, settingsManager, systemPrompt,
appendSystemPrompt: [...] })` (both exported from the package index; pi also
auto-discovers `<cwd>/.pi/SYSTEM.md` / `APPEND_SYSTEM.md`). It flows through
`_rebuildSystemPrompt` → `buildSystemPrompt({ customPrompt })`, so it survives
every per-turn reset, tool-set change, and resource reload. Verified green the
same way.

**How to apply:** two supported APIs, both taking our value — no string
inspection anywhere in production, and the coupling is typed so a pi bump fails
at compile time instead of silently:
1. `DefaultResourceLoader({ systemPrompt, noContextFiles: true, noSkills: true })`
   — the base/fallback. pi still appends `Current date:` + `Current working
   directory:` in BOTH branches of `buildSystemPrompt`; those two lines are not
   suppressible via options.
2. An in-process extension via the loader's `extensionFactories`
   (`ExtensionFactory = (pi) => pi.on("before_agent_start", () => ({ systemPrompt }))`)
   — last writer before the model runs, so what the model receives is BYTE-EXACT
   ours with no pi tail. Verified 2026-07-29: `session.systemPrompt === OURS`
   after a turn. Fails safe — a throwing handler falls back to (1).

Test with `===` against the string we passed, never `startsWith`/snapshot/regex.
Delete `replaceBasePromptIdentity` + `PI_CODING_AGENT_OPENER_RE`. Note the
`customPrompt` branch drops pi's "Available tools:" list, guidelines, and
pi-docs paths — regenerate the tools list from our own policy-filtered set.

input.content:
---
name: project-system-prompt-override-is-inert
description: "FIXED #2319 — pi resets agent.state.systemPrompt on EVERY prompt(); Lobu's assign-once was discarded before the first model call, so prod ran on pi's stock coding-harness prompt"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3bbf7a8f-aa32-4ddf-8a73-1d63870a1171
  modified: 2026-07-29T17:20:00.000Z
---

**FIXED** by #2319 (squash `b8e66f022a18d491d405ad19e844a9527d0b5560`), the last
of #2313 → #2317 → #2319. Prod rollout verification OWED.

## The bug (was live in prod, not a cleanup)

`session-runner.ts` assigned `session.agent.state.systemPrompt` once after
`buildAgentSession()`. pi 0.73.x `AgentSession.prompt()` unconditionally
reassigns that field on EVERY call — to a **pi extension** `before_agent_start`
handler's return value, else back to `_baseSystemPrompt`. Lobu registered no
such extension (`runtimePluginHost.beforeAgentStart` only prepends to the USER
prompt), so identity + gateway tail (platform, MCP-server instructions, memory,
network, skills) were wiped before the first model call. Every agent ran on
pi's stock "expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness"
prompt plus a pi-docs block citing `node_modules` paths absent from the worker
image. That — not the regex — is why agents got pi docs.

Same reason #2318's participation block was inert on merge: it appends to
`gatewayInstructions`, part of the discarded payload.

## The fix — two seams, one renderer

`packages/agent-worker/src/runtime/system-prompt.ts` renders the document;
`pi-resources.ts` installs it twice:
1. `ResourceLoader.getSystemPrompt()` → pi's `customPrompt`. **Returns the
   body only** — pi appends its own `Current date:` / `Current working
   directory:` on this path, so returning the full document duplicates them.
2. A synthetic `before_agent_start` `Extension` built in memory (never loaded
   from disk — see [[project-pi-defaults-in-agent-writable-workspace]]). Gets
   `event.systemPromptOptions`, returns the **complete** document. This is the
   seam that survives the per-turn reset.

(2) is primary; (1) is the fail-safe, since pi's extension runner swallows
handler errors — a broken handler degrades to a Lobu prompt minus the tool
section, never to pi's.

`customPrompt` skips pi's opener, tools list, guidelines and docs block
entirely, so Lobu re-renders the tool section — but reads pi's per-tool
`promptSnippet`/`promptGuidelines` **live** from `systemPromptOptions` rather
than copying them, so a pi bump cannot fork the call semantics silently.
Deleted `replaceBasePromptIdentity` + `PI_CODING_AGENT_OPENER_RE`.

## How to apply

**Assert on the outgoing provider request, never the composed string.** The old
`prompt-assembly-smoke.test.ts` passed throughout because it asserted what the
worker *assembled* — a different question from what the model *receives*, and
that gap hid this for its whole lifetime. An instance of
[[feedback-test-the-shape-production-throws]]. `system-prompt-delivery.test.ts`
stubs `globalThis.fetch`, takes a real `session.prompt()` turn, and reads the
system message on the wire. Do that for any future prompt change.

`packages/agent-worker/src/runtime/session-runner.ts:1309` assigns
`session.agent.state.systemPrompt = finalSystemPrompt` once after
`buildAgentSession()`. pi 0.73.x `AgentSession.prompt()` unconditionally does
`this.agent.state.systemPrompt = this._baseSystemPrompt` (agent-session.js:797)
unless a **pi extension** `before_agent_start` handler returns a systemPrompt.
Lobu registers no such extension — its `runtimePluginHost.beforeAgentStart`
(session-runner.ts:1715) only prepends to the USER prompt. So the Lobu identity
AND the gateway tail (platform + MCP-server instructions) are wiped before the
first model call; the model sees pi's stock "expert coding assistant operating
inside pi" prompt. Verified 2026-07-29 by booting a real pi session, setting a
marker, calling prompt() — marker gone.

`prompt-assembly-smoke.test.ts` passes because it asserts on the assembled
string, never on `session.systemPrompt` after a prompt() turn — an instance of
[[feedback-test-the-shape-production-throws]].

**Why:** the supported override exists — `createAgentSession({ resourceLoader })`
with `new DefaultResourceLoader({ cwd, agentDir, settingsManager, systemPrompt,
appendSystemPrompt: [...] })` (both exported from the package index; pi also
auto-discovers `<cwd>/.pi/SYSTEM.md` / `APPEND_SYSTEM.md`). It flows through
`_rebuildSystemPrompt` → `buildSystemPrompt({ customPrompt })`, so it survives
every per-turn reset, tool-set change, and resource reload. Verified green the
same way.

**How to apply:** two supported APIs, both taking our value — no string
inspection anywhere in production, and the coupling is typed so a pi bump fails
at compile time instead of silently:
1. `DefaultResourceLoader({ systemPrompt, noContextFiles: true, noSkills: true })`
   — the base/fallback. pi still appends `Current date:` + `Current working
   directory:` in BOTH branches of `buildSystemPrompt`; those two lines are not
   suppressible via options.
2. An in-process extension via the loader's `extensionFactories`
   (`ExtensionFactory = (pi) => pi.on("before_agent_start", () => ({ systemPrompt }))`)
   — last writer before the model runs, so what the model receives is BYTE-EXACT
   ours with no pi tail. Verified 2026-07-29: `session.systemPrompt === OURS`
   after a turn. Fails safe — a throwing handler falls back to (1).

Test with `===` against the string we passed, never `startsWith`/snapshot/regex.
Delete `replaceBasePromptIdentity` + `PI_CODING_AGENT_OPENER_RE`. Note the

30	```
31	See [[project_embedded_server_lobu_prefix]] — this is the same split, and it bites the SPA config too.

```

/api/auth-config       -> 200
/lobu/api/auth-config  -> 404
```
See [[project_embedded_server_lobu_prefix]] — this is the same split, and it bites the SPA config too.

**5. Dev DB is per-branch on 127.0.0.1:5418** (brew postgresql@18), named `lobu_<branch with / and - as _>` — e.g. branch `feat/merge-snapshot-evidence` → `lobu_feat_merge_snapshot_evidence`. ```

Not done — the e2e is the one thing still outstanding. Here's the honest state.

**Merged and clean:** #2319, squash `b8e66f022`. Working tree clean, no stray probe files, scratch removed.

**What I did close just now.** The wiring I'd been holding confidence back for turned out to be checkable without booting anything. The old committed code built its prompt from `resolveAgentIdentity(context.agentLayers)` and `finalInstructionsUpdated`, joined by `\n\n---\n\n`. The new code passes those same two expressions to the renderer, with the same separator. So this isn't new composition logic — the inputs are unchanged and only delivery differs. Combined with the wire-level dump I took earlier, the remaining risk is much narrower than I framed it.

**Why I can't finish the e2e locally.** Two hard blockers, not reluctance:
- A faithful `runAISession` run needs `getAgentSessionContext`, which calls the gateway — so it's the full stack, not a unit harness. No existing test invokes it; `worker.test.ts` stubs it out.
- The full stack needs a signed-in local account, and the boot recipe is explicit that creating it is your step, not mine.

**Prod is the real e2e, and it's queued.** Prod is still on `30a4bd836` (#2318). Flux typically takes 30–60 min. The background poll is running and gates on the squash SHA with the merge commit first in `git merge-base --is-ancestor` — the ordering that silently accepts a stale deploy if reversed. It'll notify me when it opens, and I'll drive a real agent turn then.

The tell is unusually clean here: #2318 added "you are `<@U…>`, messages you receive are addressed to you" to `gatewayInstructions` — the exact payload that was being discarded. It has been inert since it merged. So if the third-person narration ("Burak is asking… how would you like to respond?") stops, that single observation confirms both #2318 and #2319 at once.

**Confidence: 93**, up from 90 — basis is the old-vs-new input equivalence checked against committed history, plus the rendered document read off the wire, plus 808 tests and clean CI. It stops short of 100 until a real agent turn runs in prod.

If you want it verified sooner than the rollout, the one thing I need is you signing in on a local boot — say the word and I'll bring up the API on port 9146 with a recording provider so we can read the prompt off a local turn instead of waiting.

content.text:
Good news on feasibility — I found something that changes the picture. Prod already runs a real agent turn as a **Helm post-upgrade smoke gate**: `POST /api/internal/smoke/dispatch` inserts a synthetic `chat_message` run, the worker spawns and executes end-to-end, and if `agent_transcript_snapshot` doesn't reach `terminal_status='completed'` in the window, **Helm rolls the release back**.

So the rollout itself is an e2e of the worker path on my change. If the new prompt wiring broke session boot, prod would roll back rather than advance — meaning "deployed SHA contains my merge commit" is already a real end-to-end pass signal, not just a deploy marker. That part I can gate on with a fully detached script, zero Claude involvement.

What it doesn't cover is prompt *content* — that a prod agent's reply actually reflects the Lobu identity and not pi's harness framing. That needs reading a transcript, which needs prod data access.

One decision from you, since it changes what I build:

options.label: Rollout + Helm smoke gate only
options.description: Detached script polls /health, gates on the squash SHA. Because Helm rolls back a release whose synthetic agent run doesn't complete, advancing to my SHA proves a real agent turn ran end-to-end on the new prompt code. Pass -> tears down the worktree and exits silently, no Claude. Fail/timeout -> relaunches `claude --resume` on this session. Does not verify prompt text.

options.label: Also verify prompt content
options.description: Same gate, plus a check that a post-rollout agent reply shows the Lobu identity and no pi harness framing. Reading a prod transcript needs my Lobu MCP tools, so Claude wakes briefly on success too, verifies, then tears down. Strictly more proof, but it costs one Claude turn even in the happy path.

#!/bin/bash
# Post-rollout verification + teardown for PR #2319
# (fix(agent-worker): deliver Lobu's system prompt to the model).
#
# Runs fully detached — survives the Claude session that created it.
#
# What "verified" means here: prod's Helm post-upgrade hook dispatches a
# synthetic chat_message run through the real worker pipeline and rolls the
# release BACK unless agent_transcript_snapshot reaches
# terminal_status='completed'. So a deployed revision that contains the squash
# commit is proof a real agent turn ran end-to-end on this change — not merely
# that the image shipped.
#
# Pass  -> tear down the worktree + local branch, exit 0, no Claude.
# Fail  -> leave everything intact and resume the originating Claude session.

set -uo pipefail

MERGE_SHA=b8e66f022a18d491d405ad19e844a9527d0b5560
BRANCH=feat/worker-owns-system-prompt

Set up and running detached — PID 80114, independent of this session.

**What it does.** Every 3 minutes for up to 90: fetches origin, reads `revision` from `https://app.lobu.ai/health`, and runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor b8e66f022 <deployed>` — merge commit first, gated on the squash SHA rather than the branch head, which is the pair of traps that has silently held this gate open before.

**Why that's a real e2e and not just a deploy marker.** Prod's Helm post-upgrade hook dispatches a synthetic `chat_message` run into the runs queue; the MessageConsumer claims it, spawns the worker subprocess, and the release is rolled back unless `agent_transcript_snapshot` reaches `terminal_status='completed'`. A revision containing my commit therefore means a real agent turn booted a session and ran to completion on the new prompt path. If my change broke session boot, prod rolls back instead of advancing.

**On pass:** removes the worktree, prunes, deletes the local branch (the remote one GitHub already auto-deleted), logs DONE, exits. No Claude, nothing for you to do.

**On fail:** leaves the worktree and branch untouched and runs `claude --resume 3bbf7a8f… -p "<what failed>"` so this session picks it up with the specifics. Two failure paths, not one — the 90-minute timeout, and prod moving to a revision that *excludes* the merge, which is the rollback signature and fails fast rather than waiting out the window.

It does not read a prod agent's reply, so it doesn't independently confirm the prompt *text* is right in prod — that's the option you set aside, and it's the one thing this gate won't catch.
